items.title: Australia to send surveillance plane to help 'protect and secure' airspace in the Gulf
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has confirmed the Australian Defence Force will deploy an E-7A Wedgetail aircraft to the Gulf to help protect and defend the region, providing long-range reconnaissance activity.

items.title: Live: Trump says war could be over soon, Iran says his comments are 'nonsense'
items.description: Iranian politicians and institutions have issued pledges of loyalty to the new supreme leader. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Coalition welcomes humanitarian visas for Iranian football players
items.description: The Coalition welcomes Labor's decision to issue humanitarian visas to five Iranian football players who sought asylum in Australia. Follow live.

items.title: 'Welcome to stay': Five Iranian football players granted asylum in Australia
items.description: Five members of the Iranian women's soccer team, who were labelled "traitors" on Iranian state TV, have been granted asylum after fears they would be targeted by the Iranian regime if they returned home.

items.title: What you need to know about Iran today, with Laura Tingle
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor Laura Tingle is in Dubai and will provide daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: In the early hours of the Iran war, Indonesia's president made a telling offer
items.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's big ambitions on the world stage and at home have alarmed his critics.

items.title: Dubai's 'cringe' influencers have a new rule: Don't mention the war
items.description: As missiles and drones began lighting up the sky over Dubai, many of the city's social media personalities started posting about it. Then the government stepped in.

items.title: Labor to pass super tax changes with support of Greens
items.description: The legislation comes as speculation builds that the federal government will pursue more ambitious tax changes in the May budget.

items.title: Will this year's flu vaccine protect against the fast-moving Super-K strain?
items.description: Experts say they are feeling "nervous" as Australia approached this year's flu season, with a new, fast-moving strain of influenza dubbed "Super-K" circulating as vaccine uptake dwindles.

items.title: Officials intercept 150,000 melatonin units at border, amid broader crackdown
items.description: Australian Border Force officials have intercepted more than 150,000 units of melatonin in four months, after authorities warned they would crack down on unregulated products.

items.title: Live: ASX rises after heavy sell-off as oil prices moderate
items.description: The Australian market is tracking higher after Wall Street's overnight rise. The ASX 200 is up 1.5 per cent, regaining some of yesterday's losses, spurred by concerns about the impact of the Middle East war. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Live: Water creeps up in Bundaberg amid major flood warning
items.description: A major flood is threatening Bundaberg after days of rain spilled dams and set rivers on the rise across Queensland.

items.title: Unwell, elderly blocking hospital beds due to lack of GP home visits
items.description: The number of GP home visits has declined by 85 per cent in Australia over the past three decades, which doctors say is driving vulnerable people into residential care and hospital prematurely.

items.title: Industry that moves 'everything you buy in shops' under major pressure
items.description: Increasing fuel prices are putting pressure on the road transport industry, with the potential to impact the price of everything from furniture to food.

items.title: From cattle stations to city streets, how cowboy fashion went mainstream
items.description: From streetwear to festival fits, country fashion has become mainstream in Australian cities and heritage brands are reaping the benefits.

items.title: AI's assault on creatives put to the sword in new play
items.description: Never mind artificial intelligence, this is dragon intelligence. A new play commissioned for the Perth Festival explores the importance of human creativity, even if AI can help with an unfinished novel.

items.title: ABC Shakespeare quiz: How well doest thou know his characters and quotes?
items.description: A quiz by any other word would smell as sweet, or something, so have a crack at our 10 questions on the works of William Shakespeare.

items.title: Darwin residents urged to reduce water usage as city's dam stops operations
items.description: Amid issues with the pump station at Darwin River Dam, which is the city's major supplier of water, Power and Water Corporation have urged locals to reduce their water consumption.

items.title: The network of Liberals behind two 'grassroots' childcare campaigns
items.description: The childcare groups say they are the voices for everyday parents. What they do not mention is that they are supported by a network of current and former Liberals.

items.title: Rainforest river cruise boat found on Great Barrier Reef after flash flood
items.description: Operators in the world heritage Daintree Rainforest are anxious about lost business after tour boats and ferries were damaged in floods ahead of the Easter holidays.

items.title: Maggie Gyllenhaal's Franken-feminist fable fumbles the plot
items.description: The Bride!, a modern retelling of The Bride of Frankenstein, takes massive swings in terms of performances, plotting and subtext, but not all of its gambles pay off.

items.title: Millions seized by Hungary from Ukrainian state bank employees
items.description: Hungary has seized around $115 million and gold from a Ukrainian bank transfer and temporarily detained seven Ukrainians, as Budapest pressures Kyiv to restart oil shipments from Russia.

items.title: Bomb found near anti-Islam protest an 'act of ISIS-inspired terrorism', NY police say
items.description: A homemade bomb thrown near an anti-Islam protest in New York at the weekend is being investigated as an Islamic State-inspired act of "terrorism," police say.

items.title: Mardi Gras pioneer wants more inclusive venues in country towns
items.description: After taking part in the original 1978 Mardi Gras parade, Kevin Betts returned to his country roots and set about making life easier for people growing up queer in the regions.

items.title: Forwarded email a rare public glimpse into the cunning world of political spin
items.description: It is common for media advisors to provide reporters with background information in an effort to shape the way a story is reported, but the practice backfired spectacularly when the SA government shared an email from the wrong patient.
